tasks.note: Browsing 2018 was printing 2026 preseason ranks on teams ESPN left unranked — a 4-5 Tennessee showed as #18 because that is its 2026 preseason spot, sitting next to a genuinely #18 Mississippi State. Fixed by asking the DATA, not the date: ESPN fills 99 for every team in an unplayed week and backfills real ranks once it is played, so a rank in 1-25 anywhere in the week means that week has its own poll and it wins. A season-equality check would still have been wrong in November, looking back at Week 3.

tasks.title: devices.html — a mobile harness that actually works
tasks.note: Window resizing did not give a true mobile viewport (page kept rendering at 1153px), so the harness iframes the pages at 375/390/430 instead. It loads them ONE AT A TIME: three iframes pulling ten ES modules at once overwhelms python -m http.server, some module requests never land, and the app then never boots — which looks exactly like an app bug and is not one.

tasks.title: Catch CFBD answering "unknown team" as "never met"
tasks.note: /teams/matchup returns team1=null and 0-0-0 for a team it cannot resolve — byte-identical to its answer for two teams that genuinely never played. Confirmed by querying a made-up school and getting the same response. The first run wrote 30 false 'never met' rows. Fixed by resolving both names against CFBD's own /teams roster BEFORE asking, so zero games is only recorded as 'First meeting' when both schools are known; anything unresolved is stored as resolved:false and renders nothing.

tasks.title: Label the odds with whose book they are
tasks.note: ESPN carries exactly one book (DraftKings) and the card was printing its number bare, which reads as a consensus. It is now tagged with the book's name, and would read 'avg of N' if more than one ever appears.

tasks.title: Preflight the CFBD quota before spending it
tasks.note: /info returns 200 even at quota 0, so it is a free meter. The builder now reads remainingCalls BEFORE it starts and refuses rather than walking into a wall. Reading X-CallLimit-Remaining off a response only tells you after the call is already spent.

tasks.title: Climate normals for games past the forecast horizon
tasks.note: Brien's ask. Open-Meteo's archive API is keyless and CORS-open, and ONE call returns a decade (3,653 days, ~104 KB) per venue. tools/build-normals.py reduces that to a per-date normal — mean high, mean low, and the share of days with measurable rain — over a +/-3 day window so one freak afternoon cannot define a date. Cards past the 16-day horizon now read 'Usually 76/57, rain on 40% of days' instead of only 'forecast opens in N days'. Labelled 10-YR NORMAL and styled quieter, because it is history, not a prediction.

tasks.title: Treat a rate-limit WINDOW as different from a throttle
tasks.note: Open-Meteo answers a spent hour with 'Hourly API request limit exceeded' — so backing off 20/40/60/80s stays inside the same hour and cannot help. Exactly the mistake already fixed for CFBD's monthly quota, repeated because I did not carry the lesson across. The normals builder now stops on an hour/day window and says to re-run later; only a short burst-throttle is waited out. 62 of 144 venues built; it resumes.

tasks.title: Turn on push protection so this cannot recur
Delete the 2018 key from Google Cloud project 599067003646
tasks.note:
NOT a repo task — the repo side is finished (keys redacted at HEAD in 6803be8, GitHub alert resolved as revoked, no live key at HEAD). This is entirely in Google Cloud.
The project was identified by probing APIs the key was never scoped for: Books and Translation both answer 'has not been used in project 599067003646', which leaks the project AND proves the key still resolves — a DELETED key returns 'API key not valid' instead. Maps only ever said 'enable Billing', which is why deletion looked ambiguous.
Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials?project=599067003646 and delete the API key row. Then Claude can confirm: the error should change from 'billing'/'not been used in project' to 'API key not valid'.
